reference_rows_limit.purpose: How many source rows the generator reads as its reference sample (n). Every profile, pool seed and validation baseline is estimated from these rows.
reference_rows_limit.up: A smaller DKW band (four times the rows per halving), better tails and rare categories. A new digest makes the run cold: every pool and chunk rebuilds, and driver memory and profiling time grow linearly.
reference_rows_limit.down: A cheaper sample query and a smaller leak surface, but rare categories and tails vanish first. Cardinality stays truncated at n either way.
reference_rows_limit.tip: Raise it when a tail or a rare category matters and expect a cold run; answer cardinality with --source_stats exact, never with a bigger sample.

refs.label: Dvoretzky, Kiefer & Wolfowitz 1956 — the DKW inequality
Article 2 — the 10k sample, its knobs and their aftermath

source_stats.purpose: Which source-stats tier the profiler writes: off, sample (the reference sample, free) or exact (one aggregate scan of the live table).
source_stats.up: exact adds HLL++ distinct, deciles and top-k over the whole table, and the exact distinct count sizes the free-text pool target. One BigQuery scan of the source per run.
source_stats.down: off writes no stats rows, no JSON and no pool hints; engines still profile per worker. sample is free, but every distinct count is capped at the rows the sample saw.
source_stats.tip: A failed exact scan degrades loudly to the sample tier (milestone source_stats_exact_failed) and never kills the run.

top_values_max_distinct.purpose: Literal source values land in the stats only for enum-like columns with at most this many distinct values. Above it a column gets shapes, entropy and lengths, never values.
top_values_max_distinct.up: More columns store literal values in the stats table: the exemplar-leak surface grows.
top_values_max_distinct.down: Fewer literal values; more columns are described by shape and entropy only.
top_values_max_distinct.tip: It mirrors the engines' free-text category cap, so “enum-routed” means the same thing everywhere.

refs.label: Carlini et al. 2021 — extracting training data

top_values_top_k.purpose: How many literal top values an enum-like column keeps in its stats entry.
top_values_top_k.up: More of the head of the distribution is visible in the stats row.
top_values_top_k.down: A smaller stats row; the tail of an enum is summarised by entropy only.
top_values_top_k.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

shape_mix_top_k.purpose: How many character-shape masks (9 digit, A upper, a lower) a column's source_table_stats entry keeps, with their shares. The engines build their own shape mixes and never read it.
shape_mix_top_k.up: The stats entry records more of a long-tailed format's minority masks; generation does not change.
shape_mix_top_k.down: The stats entry keeps only the dominant masks; generation does not change.
shape_mix_top_k.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

length_percentiles.purpose: The three length quantiles a string column's source_table_stats entry records, under the fixed names len_p05, len_p50 and len_p95. The pool prompt's length hint has its own fixed p05–p95 band and never reads these.
length_percentiles.up: A wider band records more of the length tails in the stats entry; prompts and generation do not change.
length_percentiles.down: A tighter band records only typical lengths in the stats entry; prompts and generation do not change.
length_percentiles.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

null_pattern_max_cols.purpose: Tables wider than this skip the row null-pattern pass, which costs O(rows × columns).
null_pattern_max_cols.up: Wide tables get their joint null structure measured, at a pass whose alphabet grows with width.
null_pattern_max_cols.down: More tables fall back to per-column null rates only.
null_pattern_max_cols.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

null_pattern_top_k.purpose: How many row null patterns (which columns are null together) the __table__ entry keeps.
null_pattern_top_k.up: More of the joint null structure is recorded.
null_pattern_top_k.down: Only the most common patterns survive.
null_pattern_top_k.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

engine.purpose: Which GenerationEngine runs, by its ENGINE_REGISTRY name: b1_rag (retrieval plus bounded LLM pools) or b2_library (the sdgx wrapper).
engine.up: b2_library fits a library model once per worker and keeps more joint structure; numerics interpolate through 11 deciles.
engine.down: b1_rag samples marginals from the whole sorted sample and seeds LLM pools by retrieval.
engine.tip: Both engines sit behind one interface, so the pipeline, validation and audit are identical; swap with the flag.

num_rows.purpose: Rows to generate (M) for a root table. A driven child derives its count from its parent's landed keys times the measured fan-out (ADR 0036).
num_rows.up: More rows reuse each pool value more often and tighten identifier keyspaces; time grows linearly.
num_rows.down: Faster runs; the fidelity per row does not change, because the sample, not M, sets the error.
num_rows.tip: M never enters the sampling-error formula: it only raises the cost of being wrong.

similarity.purpose: A 0–1 dial the engines interpret differently: b2 maps it to sampling temperatures, b1 only blends its temporal draws.
similarity.up: b2: colder categorical sampling and a lower LLM temperature, output closer to the reference. b1: temporal draws anchored nearer observed instants.
similarity.down: b2: hotter sampling, more divergence. b1: temporal draws closer to uniform over the range.
similarity.tip: Numeric, categorical and free-text draws of b1 ignore it at the exported commit (see Docs differ).

seed.purpose: An explicit base RNG seed; empty derives one per (run_id, batch_id), so runs never replay across triggers.
seed.up: A fixed seed replays the same draws for the same run inputs — useful for A/B runs and goldens.
seed.down: Empty (default) keeps every trigger's draws independent.

batch_size.purpose: Rows per Beam element. At the default it scales with --num_rows toward about 1,000 elements, never below 16.
batch_size.up: Fewer, larger elements amortise per-element Python overhead over vectorized draws; a failed batch loses more rows.
batch_size.down: More elements, more per-element overhead: 16 rows per element made a 1M-row run pay it 62,500 times.
batch_size.tip: Pass a value only to pin it; the default already scales.

temporal_max_age_years_b1.purpose: b1 clamps the jitter floor of generated dates to now minus this many years; fully historical columns keep their observed range.
temporal_max_age_years_b1.down: A tighter window pushes generated instants toward the present.
temporal_max_age_years_b1.tip: Interim policy: per-column DDL-JSON descriptions will override the constant later.

temporal_max_age_years_b2.purpose: b2's floor for generated dates and timestamps: max(observed min, now minus this many years). A column whose whole range is older keeps it.
temporal_max_age_years_b2.down: A tighter window; the decile vector's sub-floor points collapse onto the floor.
temporal_max_age_years_b2.tip: Interim policy: per-column DDL-JSON descriptions will override the constant later.

free_text_pool_max.purpose: The most distinct values a free-text pool can hold, shared by both engines' ladders and the launcher's PK-capacity preflight. A PK routed to a pool caps at it.
free_text_pool_max.up: More diversity per column, at LLM cost linear in the pool size.
free_text_pool_max.down: Cheaper pools; M rows reuse each value M/cap times.
free_text_pool_max.tip: Identifiers never come from pools: shape expansion and keyspace generation carry them.

pool_values_per_call.purpose: Values requested per LLM call: one JSON-array completion.
pool_values_per_call.up: Fewer round trips per pool, longer completions per call.
pool_values_per_call.down: More round trips; each call is shorter and cheaper to retry.
pool_values_per_call.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

pool_parallel_choices.purpose: Independent completions (vLLM n=) per HTTP round trip, de-duplicated across choices. It multiplies novel yield per call about four times.
pool_parallel_choices.up: More yield per round trip; more sequences in flight on the GPU.
pool_parallel_choices.down: Less parallel sampling; more round trips.
pool_parallel_choices.tip: Safe because pool requests are unseeded, and the prompt stays byte-identical (prefix-cache friendly).

pool_stagnation_window.purpose: Once every escalation level has run, this many consecutive low-yield attempts end a pool ladder.
pool_stagnation_window.up: Ladders keep trying longer against decaying yield.
pool_stagnation_window.down: Ladders stop sooner; a slow-but-productive column may end undersized.
pool_stagnation_window.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

pool_stagnation_min_novel.purpose: An attempt that adds fewer novel values than this counts toward stagnation.
pool_stagnation_min_novel.up: Stricter: more attempts count as stagnant, ladders end sooner.
pool_stagnation_min_novel.down: Looser: a trickle of novel values keeps a ladder alive.
pool_stagnation_min_novel.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

pool_format_collapse_rounds.purpose: Consecutive full-yield rounds with zero in-format values that end a ladder (a structural mismatch temperature cannot fix).
pool_format_collapse_rounds.up: More wasted rounds before the shape fallback takes over.
pool_format_collapse_rounds.down: Faster exit to the shape fallback, less tolerance for a noisy first round.
pool_format_collapse_rounds.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

pool_build_max_workers.purpose: How many column ladders run in parallel on a thread pool; vLLM continuous-batches the concurrent requests.
pool_build_max_workers.up: More concurrency, until the GPU's KV cache queues the extra sequences.
pool_build_max_workers.down: Closer to sequential ladders: setup time grows with the number of free-text columns.
pool_build_max_workers.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

source_domain_cap.purpose: The largest source-distinct set kept as a worker-side rejection filter against copies. Above it the engine degrades loudly to sample-only rejection.
source_domain_cap.up: High-cardinality columns keep full-domain copy rejection, at tens of MB of worker memory per million strings.
source_domain_cap.down: More columns fall back to rejecting only what the sample saw.
source_domain_cap.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

free_text_unique_ratio.purpose: A string column whose unique share exceeds this, with a long mean length, routes to free text instead of categorical.
free_text_unique_ratio.up: Fewer columns reach the LLM pool.
free_text_unique_ratio.down: More columns reach the LLM pool, including repetitive ones.
free_text_unique_ratio.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

free_text_min_mean_len.purpose: The mean rendered length above which a high-unique string column is free text.
free_text_min_mean_len.up: Short unique strings stay categorical or shaped.
free_text_min_mean_len.down: Short unique strings route to the pool.
free_text_min_mean_len.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

free_text_max_categories.purpose: Above this distinct count a string column is high-cardinality and treated as free text even if short.
free_text_max_categories.up: More columns stay categorical (sampled from their observed values).
free_text_max_categories.down: More columns become free text or shaped identifiers.
free_text_max_categories.tip: The profiler's literal top-values cap mirrors it.

freetext_expansion.purpose: The shape-preserving expander after pool draws: off (pool draws only), identifiers (code-like columns expand from their shape mix) or all.
freetext_expansion.up: all also mutates digit runs inside texty draws: more distinct values, never an LLM call.
freetext_expansion.down: off caps every free-text column's distinct count at the pool size.
freetext_expansion.tip: The default, identifiers, is what keeps a 90M-row run from repeating 512 codes.

pool_seed_strategy.purpose: How the 8 prompt seeds are chosen: centroid (densest region), kcenter (spans the column's modes) or kcenter_rotate (re-seeded per attempt).
pool_seed_strategy.up: kcenter and kcenter_rotate widen coverage of rare modes; rotate forfeits vLLM prefix caching by design.
pool_seed_strategy.down: centroid (control) keeps a byte-identical prefix and conditions on the densest region.

prompt_constraints.purpose: Attach each column's llm_prompt_constraint and measured length band to pool prompts, as a constant suffix.
prompt_constraints.up: on: prompts follow the declared format; the shared prefix stays cacheable.
prompt_constraints.down: off: prompts rely on exemplars alone.

prompt_debug.purpose: Log each built pool prompt as a milestone: off, redacted (seed exemplars elided) or full.
prompt_debug.up: full logs verbatim prompts at WARNING: reference values reach Dataflow logs. Debug runs only.

pool_pattern_guidance.purpose: Constrain identifier-ish pool completions at decode time with a charset and length regex (vLLM structured output).
pool_pattern_guidance.up: true: fewer off-format values reach the post-hoc gate, at an unmeasured T4 throughput cost.
pool_pattern_guidance.down: empty or false (default): the post-hoc format gate alone protects pools.

build_pool_layer.purpose: Build free-text pools in their own branch and persist them (skipped when this reference digest and model are already stored).
build_pool_layer.up: true: pools are built once and every worker reads them (warm runs skip the LLM); a no-op without freetext_pools_table.
build_pool_layer.down: empty: pools are inferred inside every worker process's setup().

rag_row_docs_limit.purpose: How many fingerprint-ordered reference rows are embedded as row documents: exactly the rows the engine reads back.
rag_row_docs_limit.up: More rows in the in-worker index and more population cost; a value above the reference sample is clamped to it.
rag_row_docs_limit.down: A smaller index that covers fewer of the sample's modes.
rag_row_docs_limit.tip: One value for writer and reader. A chunk store written with a smaller value is topped up with the missing rows.

max_free_text_values_per_column.purpose: Distinct (column, value) chunks embedded per free-text column; a near-unique column stays bounded here.
max_free_text_values_per_column.up: More candidates for the top-8 exemplar pick, more embedding work.
max_free_text_values_per_column.down: Fewer candidates; rare values are less likely to be seeds.
max_free_text_values_per_column.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

rag_top_k.purpose: Exemplars retrieved to seed each free-text pool prompt.
rag_top_k.up: Longer prompts with more context; exemplar echoes become more likely.
rag_top_k.down: Shorter prompts, less diversity to condition on.
rag_top_k.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

bge_max_length.purpose: Tokens bge-small reads per chunk; longer serialized rows are truncated.
bge_max_length.up: Fixed by the checkpoint's position embeddings.
bge_max_length.down: Truncates more of each serialized row.

embedder_min_free_vram.purpose: Free VRAM required before the embedder's auto device picks CUDA over CPU.
embedder_min_free_vram.up: The embedder yields the GPU more often (safer next to vLLM).
embedder_min_free_vram.down: More CUDA embeds, and a real OOM risk when the card is already spoken for.
embedder_min_free_vram.tip: cuda.is_available() answers “does a GPU exist”, never “is there room”.

embedder_uri.purpose: gs:// path of the B.1 RAG embedder's weights; empty uses the HashingEmbedder.
embedder_uri.up: Setting it loads bge-small from GCS (never the Hub) for semantic retrieval.
embedder_uri.down: Empty: hashing vectors, no model download, lexical neighbours only.

build_rag_layer.purpose: Populate synthetic_rag.rag_chunks from this run's reference sample (skipped when the digest is already present for this embedder).
build_rag_layer.up: true: chunks and vectors persist, and later runs read them instead of re-embedding; a no-op without rag_chunks_table.
build_rag_layer.down: empty: the engine embeds its 1,024 rows in setup on every fresh digest.

env.purpose: The threshold tier (dev, uat, prd) that selects the BLOCKER ratio a run may reach before it fails.

uniqueness_mode.purpose: How duplicates are handled before landing: exact (one full-row shuffle barrier), exact_chained (the older three-barrier chain) or streaming (measure, do not remove).
uniqueness_mode.up: exact_chained: three shuffles per table, kept for A/B runs only.
uniqueness_mode.down: streaming: no barrier between generation and BigQuery; duplicate rows land and the run still fails the gate.
uniqueness_mode.tip: exact is the default and removes every duplicate behind one barrier.

driven_uniqueness_mode.purpose: The uniqueness mode for a driven child without identity columns: its PK is unique by construction, so streaming measures without a barrier.
driven_uniqueness_mode.up: exact adds a barrier the construction already made unnecessary.
driven_uniqueness_mode.down: streaming (default) lands rows without the landing-path shuffle.

write_disposition.purpose: Landing-table write mode: append (WRITE_APPEND) or overwrite (WRITE_TRUNCATE).
write_disposition.up: overwrite replaces the table: the re-run after a streaming-mode failure.
write_disposition.down: append adds rows; the DLQ, validation_runs and rag_chunks always append.

repeat_share_tolerance.purpose: The absolute tolerance between the source's key-repeat share and the landed one, when a launch adjusted the model (ADR 0038).
repeat_share_tolerance.up: Looser verdicts on an adjusted table's copy.
repeat_share_tolerance.down: Tighter: per-key sampling noise (O(1/√keys)) may flag a faithful copy.

generate_fk_relationships.purpose: Honour declared relationships: a launch expands to the table's whole FK component, parents first, and children sample landed parent keys.
generate_fk_relationships.down: false: declared edges are ignored loudly and FK columns use marginals.

relationships_uri.purpose: Where the relationship models live: a folder or YAML file, local or gs://. The only source of relational truth.
relationships_uri.up: A gs:// path changes PK/FK without rebuilding the image.
relationships_uri.down: The default reads config/relationships packaged in the image.

multi_table_mode.purpose: How a multi-table plan runs: single_job (one fleet, one vLLM ignition, in-DAG key handoff) or sequential_jobs.
multi_table_mode.up: sequential_jobs: one job per table, parents first — a fallback for debugging.
multi_table_mode.down: single_job (default): one worker fleet for the whole component.

on_model_conflict.purpose: What a measured contradiction between the relationship model and the source does: adjust (drop the disproved PK and announce it) or stop.
on_model_conflict.up: stop refuses the launch, as before ADR 0038.
on_model_conflict.down: adjust (default) carries on and reproduces the source's key-repeat share.
on_model_conflict.tip: Self-contradictions and the PK-capacity gate stop under both settings.

fk_candidate_cap.purpose: Top-M parent candidates kept per shared value on a conditional (diamond) edge.
fk_candidate_cap.up: A wider per-key choice, and fewer keys per batch to keep a request under the value cap.
fk_candidate_cap.down: Hot shared keys wrap sooner over a shorter candidate list.

fk_key_sample_floor.purpose: The side-input cap: a child samples at most this many parent key tuples unless its PK needs more.
fk_key_sample_floor.up: Bigger side inputs per worker, fewer duplicate draws.
fk_key_sample_floor.down: Smaller side inputs; PKs built on the key draw collide sooner.
fk_key_sample_floor.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

fk_key_sample_ceiling.purpose: The largest parent-key side input the sizing will ask for (about 40 MB pickled per million single-column keys).
fk_key_sample_ceiling.up: More SDK memory per process; past it the answer is the co-partitioned join (ADR 0036).
fk_key_sample_ceiling.down: PK capacity runs out sooner on big children.
fk_key_sample_ceiling.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

fk_key_sample_margin.purpose: The capacity target over num_rows when PK members are drawn at random: at 10×, expected duplicates are about 4.8 %.
fk_key_sample_margin.up: Fewer duplicate draws, larger side inputs.
fk_key_sample_margin.down: More pk.duplicate rows diverted to the DLQ.

max_conditional_values_per_request.purpose: The most candidate values one fan-out request may carry per conditional edge; keys per batch shrink to stay under it.
max_conditional_values_per_request.down: Smaller requests; more elements for the same keys.
max_conditional_values_per_request.tip: Set it in a config file (--config_uri); a cache it shapes is rebuilt under the new value.

client_type.purpose: Which ModelClient generates: vllm (a server the worker owns), mlx (local Apple smoke) or fake (no model).
client_type.up: vllm: real free-text pools on a GPU worker.
client_type.down: fake: exercises the whole Dataflow → BigQuery path without a GPU.

vllm_dtype.purpose: vLLM's --dtype: auto (the checkpoint's), float16 or bfloat16.
vllm_dtype.down: float16 is required on T4 for bf16 checkpoints like Qwen; refused for Gemma (empty output).

vllm_max_model_len.purpose: vLLM's --max-model-len cap; without it the KV cache is sized for the checkpoint's native context.
vllm_max_model_len.up: Longer prompts fit, and the KV cache takes more VRAM (262k native context killed a T4 at startup).
vllm_max_model_len.down: Less VRAM for KV; 8,192 already dwarfs the synthesis prompts.

autoscaling.purpose: Fleet sizing: auto (pinned when --initial_workers is set), fixed (pinned, workers required) or throughput (Dataflow scales).
autoscaling.up: throughput: Dataflow scales freely; multi runs lost about 4 min per job to mid-job scale-downs.
autoscaling.down: fixed: a fleet that starts and stays full.

initial_workers.purpose: The initial Dataflow worker count; empty keeps Dataflow's own default.
initial_workers.up: A scale run starts at its max_num_workers and skips the ramp.
initial_workers.down: Empty: the R6 pair started on 2 workers and ran 8 min at a quarter of its steady rate.

gpu.purpose: The workers' GPU; a null vllm_dtype follows it.
gpu.down: t4: cheaper; float16 only, no Gemma.
gpu.tip: The Composer DAG picks the worker machine and accelerator from it (l4 or t4); the launcher derives a null vllm_dtype from it (t4 → float16, l4 → bfloat16) and records it. Gemma cannot run on a T4, and models too large for its VRAM fit only an L4.

sdk_containers.up: multi: one per vCPU, past the GIL ceiling.
sdk_containers.tip: The worker topology of a vLLM launch: the Composer DAG turns single into the no_use_multiple_sdk_containers experiment. multi lets generation escape the one-interpreter GIL ceiling (the sheet charts the measured pair); with single one process owns the GPU. A direct launch passes its experiments itself, and the launcher only records the value.

launcher_machine_type.up: Faster image pull and table prep.
launcher_machine_type.tip: The Flex Template launcher VM, not the workers. It pulls the multi-GB image, reads every table's reference sample and builds the graph inside Google's 12-minute launch limit, so a large model wants a larger one. The Composer DAG launches with it; a direct launch sets launcherMachineType itself, and the launcher only records the value.

ddl_uri.purpose: A pinned _ddl.json read only when live schema extraction fails (air-gap, BigQuery outage).
ddl_uri.up: A path: the pin is the fallback, and its staleness is reported as ddl_pin_drift.
ddl_uri.down: Empty: no fallback — a failed live extraction stops the launch.

reference_table.purpose: The source table the reference sample is SELECTed from and the schema is extracted from.
reference_table.up: Point it at another table to generate from a different source.
reference_table.down: Required with launch.tables explicit (the default) — a launch without it is refused; unused with all.

landing_table.purpose: Where valid synthetic rows land; a comma-separated list plans several tables at once.
landing_table.up: More tables in the list widen the plan to their components (one job in single_job mode).
landing_table.down: Required with launch.tables explicit (the default) — a launch without it is refused; unused with all.

dlq_table.purpose: Where rejected records land with their rule id and full error context.
dlq_table.up: Point it at another dataset to keep a run's rejects apart.
dlq_table.down: Required — a launch without it is refused.

create_if_not_exists.purpose: true creates the landing table on first write from the derived schema; anything else needs it to exist.
create_if_not_exists.up: true: a first launch creates the table, without parameterized column constraints.
create_if_not_exists.down: false: a missing landing table fails the load job.

validation_runs_table.purpose: Where each launch writes one summary row per table — the gate outcome and its provenance.
validation_runs_table.up: Set: every launch is recorded, and the evaluator can find it.
validation_runs_table.down: Empty: no summary row is written.

rag_chunks_table.purpose: The persisted embedding store B.1 reads instead of re-embedding its row documents.
rag_chunks_table.up: Set: stored vectors are read; with build_rag_layer they are also written.
rag_chunks_table.down: Empty: every worker embeds its row documents in setup.

freetext_pools_table.purpose: The persisted free-text pools workers read instead of rebuilding them.
freetext_pools_table.up: Set: stored pools are served; with build_pool_layer a branch builds missing ones.
freetext_pools_table.down: Empty: every worker process infers its own pools in setup.

fk_fanout_stats_table.purpose: Caches each driving edge's measured source fan-out so a repeat launch skips the measurement.
fk_fanout_stats_table.up: Set: a repeat launch reads the cached histogram.
fk_fanout_stats_table.down: Empty: fan-out is measured on every launch.

source_stats_table.purpose: Where per-column source stats rows are written, once per table and reference digest.
source_stats_table.up: Set: the stats are queryable after the run.
source_stats_table.down: Empty: the stats land only in the log and the JSON artifact.

source_stats_json.purpose: A gs:// or local path the source stats are also written to as one JSON file.
source_stats_json.up: Set: the stats are kept next to the run's other artifacts.

source_dataset.purpose: With launch.tables all, the project.dataset every table's source is read from under the table's own name, unless the model gives the table a source_table.
source_dataset.up: Set: a whole-model launch reads each source from this dataset.
source_dataset.down: Empty: required with launch.tables all; an explicit launch reads io.reference_table instead.

landing_dataset.purpose: With launch.tables all, the project.dataset every table lands in, under its own name.
landing_dataset.up: Set: a whole-model launch writes each table there.
landing_dataset.down: Empty: required with launch.tables all; an explicit launch writes to io.landing_table instead.

run_id.purpose: The launch's identity — it seeds batch draws when seed is empty and names every summary row.
run_id.up: A fresh id per trigger keeps retriggers from replaying the same rows.
run_id.down: Required, and a flag only — a config file may not set it.

tables.purpose: Which tables a launch generates: explicit takes io.landing_table and its components; all takes every enabled table of the one model file relational.relationships_uri names.
tables.up: all: one launch generates the whole model, in batch jobs of at most max_tables_per_job tables.
tables.down: explicit (the default): the targets and the tables their components pull in, as before.
tables.tip: Read the MODEL LAUNCH block before paying for a launch; scripts/launch/run_model.py --dry_run prints it.

max_tables_per_job.purpose: With launch.tables all, the most tables one Dataflow job generates. A connected component is never split, so a larger one gets a job of its own.
max_tables_per_job.up: Fewer, larger jobs; each launcher preps more tables inside the Flex Template's 12-minute window.
max_tables_per_job.down: More, smaller jobs; each one pays the image pull and the vLLM ignition again.
max_tables_per_job.tip: The default is an estimate; read each batch launch's margin to the 12-minute window and adjust.

max_parallel_jobs.purpose: How many batch jobs scripts/launch/run_model.py runs at once. The Composer model DAG takes its cap from the Airflow Variable SDFB_MAX_PARALLEL_JOBS instead.
max_parallel_jobs.up: The batches finish sooner; each job holds its workers' GPUs, so stay inside the GPU quota.
max_parallel_jobs.down: One at a time (the default): never more GPUs than one job asks for.

prep_workers.purpose: Threads a multi-table launcher reads schemas, reference samples and source stats on, before the cross-table steps run in plan order.
prep_workers.up: More tables read at once, and more concurrent BigQuery reads from the launcher.
prep_workers.down: 1: each table is read in turn, exactly as before ADR 0045.

batch_index.purpose: The batch of a whole-model launch this job generates (b00 is 0). The model DAG and scripts/launch/run_model.py set it.
batch_index.up: A later batch of the same plan.
batch_index.down: Unset: the launcher runs every batch itself, in sequence on the CLI (refused on Flex above one batch).

batch_count.purpose: How many batches the orchestrator planned. The launcher plans again and stops when its own count differs, because the model or K changed in between.
batch_count.up: Must equal the launcher's own plan.
batch_count.down: Unset: only together with batch_index unset.

identity_cols.purpose: Columns synthesized fresh for every row (PK, UUID), never sampled from the reference.
identity_cols.up: More columns get per-row-unique values none of which is copied from the source.
identity_cols.down: Empty: only the relationship model's identity columns apply.

pk_cols.purpose: A primary key for a table the relationship model does not cover; duplicates divert as pk.duplicate.
pk_cols.up: More columns make a wider key that fewer rows can collide on.
pk_cols.down: Empty: the relationship model decides the key.

fk_parent_landing.purpose: Expert override — the project.dataset parents landed in, when it is not the landing table's own.
fk_parent_landing.up: Set: parent keys are read from that dataset.
fk_parent_landing.down: Empty: parents are assumed to land next to the child.

model_uri.purpose: The gs:// location of the LLM weights, staged once from a model hub; config/models.yml lists them.
model_uri.up: Point it at another staged model to change the generator's LLM.
model_uri.down: Required — a launch without it is refused.

thresholds_uri.purpose: Where the per-environment severity gates are read from.
thresholds_uri.up: Point it at a gs:// copy to change the gates without rebuilding the image.
thresholds_uri.down: Unreadable: the launch falls back to a permissive gate and says so.

profiler_version.purpose: The version of profile_source_table, part of the stats table's append-skip key.
profiler_version.up: Bumping it re-profiles every table on its next run, even when the reference digest is unchanged.
profiler_version.down: Never lower it: tables already profiled at a newer version keep their rows, and stale ones stay stale.
profiler_version.tip: A constant: changing it is a code edit, a test run and an image rebuild.

generation_max_retries.purpose: GenerationConfig.max_retries, declared with a default of 2. No engine or DoFn reads it at the exported commit.
generation_max_retries.tip: Pool retries follow the sampling ladder, and a failed batch goes to the DLQ as engine_failure; neither reads this field.

hashing_embedder_dim.purpose: Dimension of the laptop HashingEmbedder (feature hashing, no model weights).
hashing_embedder_dim.up: Fewer hash collisions between tokens, more memory per vector.
hashing_embedder_dim.tip: A constant: changing it is a code edit, a test run and an image rebuild.

bge_embedder_dim.purpose: Output dimension of bge-small-en-v1.5, fixed by the model.

default_embedder_identity.purpose: The embedder name and version used when --embedder_uri is empty: the HashingEmbedder.
default_embedder_identity.up: A constant identity: chunks are keyed by it.
default_embedder_identity.down: A constant identity: chunks are keyed by it.

blocker_failure_ratio_dev.purpose: The share of rows failing a BLOCKER rule a dev run may reach before the job fails.
blocker_failure_ratio_dev.up: Looser: more defective rows are tolerated.
blocker_failure_ratio_dev.down: Stricter: fewer defective rows before FAILED_BLOCKER.
blocker_failure_ratio_dev.tip: Declared in config/thresholds.yml, not in code.

blocker_failure_ratio_uat.purpose: The share of rows failing a BLOCKER rule a uat run may reach before the job fails.
blocker_failure_ratio_uat.up: Looser: more defective rows are tolerated.
blocker_failure_ratio_uat.down: Stricter: fewer defective rows before FAILED_BLOCKER.
blocker_failure_ratio_uat.tip: Declared in config/thresholds.yml, not in code.

blocker_failure_ratio_prd.purpose: The share of rows failing a BLOCKER rule a prd run may reach before the job fails.
blocker_failure_ratio_prd.up: Looser: more defective rows are tolerated.
blocker_failure_ratio_prd.down: Stricter: fewer defective rows before FAILED_BLOCKER.
blocker_failure_ratio_prd.tip: Declared in config/thresholds.yml, not in code.

blocker_rules_declared.purpose: The rule ids config/thresholds.yml declares with severity BLOCKER.
blocker_rules_declared.up: Declaring a rule BLOCKER documents intent; only BLOCKER_RULE_IDS makes the gate count it.
blocker_rules_declared.down: Removing one changes the contract, not the gate.

blocker_rule_ids.purpose: The rule ids whose DLQ rows the BLOCKER gate counts (BLOCKER_RULE_IDS in validation/summary.py).
blocker_rule_ids.up: Counting more rules fails more runs.
blocker_rule_ids.down: A rule left out diverts rows to the DLQ without ever moving the gate.
blocker_rule_ids.tip: engine_failure is weighted by the lost batch size, not one per envelope.

temperature_ladder.purpose: The temperatures a free-text pool call escalates through when its novel yield is empty (every value a copy).
temperature_ladder.up: A higher ceiling diversifies further away from exemplar echoes, at the cost of format and plausibility.
temperature_ladder.down: Fewer escalation levels: an echo-saturated column gives up sooner.
temperature_ladder.tip: Derived by escalating_temperatures(start); 1.3 is the ceiling b2 uses for maximum divergence.

sampling_ladder.purpose: The (temperature, top_p, top_k) level of each pool attempt: the first keeps the model's own defaults, every retry escalates temperature with truncation unclamped.
sampling_ladder.up: More levels give an echoing model more chances to leave the exemplar nucleus.
sampling_ladder.down: Fewer levels: temperature alone cannot diversify a nucleus pinned by the model's generation_config.
sampling_ladder.tip: none = the served model's default; top_k 0 means all tokens in vLLM.
